What to test

All ticked. Unticking a stage skips its phases; everything a skipped stage would have produced is missing from the run, so a shorter run proves less. Reset and the report always run — a run that skipped tearing down leaves a cluster on somebody's account, and one that skipped reporting proves nothing at all.

Cluster Lifecycle E2E

not run

Twenty-one phases, in order, each knowing what it depends on and what it owes. Build openCenter-cli with mise, generate and validate a cluster configuration, deploy a Kubernetes cluster, prove Kubernetes and the platform services healthy, run smoke tests, break things on purpose, tear it all down — and prove nothing was left behind. Every button here shells into ./bin/opencenter-e2e, which is the same binary the GitHub Actions workflow calls.

The tables above ask does this command work. This asks can this build create, run and remove a platform — and only this one can notice that cluster destroy left a cluster behind, because only this one created it.

Run

Simulate produces deploy, infrastructure, Kubernetes, platform, smoke and failure-tests from a built-in fake, so every feature can be exercised before a cluster exists. Such a run can never reach PASS. Stop interrupts rather than kills, so destroy, diagnostics and the report still happen — a bench that leaks a cluster when interrupted is worse than one that takes another minute.

Troubleshooting — rerun one phase against a run that already happened. Nothing here is needed for a normal run.

A full Kind run takes about five minutes. When one phase fails you rarely want the other twenty again, so this reruns the part you care about against a run that already exists — which is exactly what the Reproduce line in every finding does: e2e phase --run-id … --only-phase smoke.

Diagnostics, destroy, verify-cleanup and report run anyway, and the seven required phases cannot be skipped: --skip-phase destroy is exactly the flag somebody reaches for when a run is slow, and it is the one that leaves a cluster running.
